items.t: openJiuwen's RSI-Native AgentOS Lets Agents Build, Install and Roll Back Their Own Plugins
items.d: openJiuwen's RSI-native AgentOS lets agents ship features as hot-pluggable, versioned extension packages. WorkSwarm agents can now write, install and roll back their own plugins.
items.x:
openJiuwen, the Huawei-backed open-source agent community, has detailed what it calls an RSI-native AgentOS: an extension mechanism designed so that AI agents can add features to their own application, try them in real work and roll them back if they break. RSI refers to recursive self-improvement. The write-up was republished by QbitAI on November 13.
The mechanism leaves extension points across five parts of the stack. Client extensions add buttons, panels and settings to the web interface. Gateway extensions handle authentication and request routing. AgentServer extensions process sessions, messages and server commands. Swarm extensions customize how multiple agents divide and hand off work and track progress. Agent extensions adjust prompts and register tools, MCP services or sub-agents.
New features ship as extension packages. Each carries a manifest.json declaring its ID, version, dependencies and code entry point, plus where any interface component should appear. On install, the system checks the manifest and stores the package by ID and version. The Gateway and AgentServer then load the packages they run and register handlers on their event buses, which fire on events such as a button click, an incoming request or the agent assembling its system prompt.

items.t: MOSS-Live Leads Six Full-Duplex Voice Metrics but Trails GPT-Live-1 on Multi-Turn Tasks
items.d: MOSS-Live tops six full-duplex metrics, wrongly answering background speech 2% of the time. It trails GPT-Live-1 on multi-turn tasks and Doubao on audio understanding.
items.x:
MOSI Intelligence and Fudan University's OpenMOSS team have published a detailed evaluation of MOSS-Live, their full-duplex real-time voice system, comparing it with OpenAI's GPT-Live-1 and GPT Realtime 2.1, ByteDance's Doubao SeedDuplex and two Qwen Audio 3.0 models. The OpenMOSS blog post, dated November 13, lays out where MOSS-Live leads and where it falls behind. All figures are vendor-published, and the post notes that sample sizes, uncertainty estimates and full test settings were not disclosed.
MOSS-Live ranked first on all six reported full-duplex metrics. It responded to speech not directed at it 2% of the time, against 68% for GPT-Live-1 and 75% for Doubao SeedDuplex. It cut in during a user's pause 1.44% of the time, against 10.37% and 14.29%. It correctly ignored irrelevant interruptions 68% of the time, compared with 21% and 13%, and held its course through brief acknowledgments such as "mm-hmm" 98.17% of the time.
Other results are mixed. On FDB v3 tool use, MOSS-Live's 51% success rate tied Doubao SeedDuplex for first and beat GPT-Live-1's 45%, but its 2.36-second response latency in tool scenarios trailed GPT Realtime 2.1 at 1.61 seconds. On the τ-Voice multi-turn task benchmark, it scored 57.93%, behind GPT-Live-1 at 67.68% and well ahead of Doubao at 17.38%.

items.t: The Endless Frontier Open-Sources Fx-Bio-1031, a Qwen-Based Model That Runs Bioinformatics Analyses
items.d: The Endless Frontier's open-weight Fx-Bio-1031 runs multi-step bioinformatics work. It reports 70.59% on BioMysteryBench's hardest subset but trails GPT-6-Astra on BixBench3.
items.x:
The Endless Frontier has released the full weights of Fx-Bio-1031, an agentic large language model for bioinformatics and computational biology, on Hugging Face. Built by post-training Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, the model is designed to plan and carry out multi-step analyses on its own: writing scripts, installing software, querying databases such as NCBI and Ensembl, and checking its own results. QbitAI reported the release on November 13.
According to the model card, Fx-Bio-1031 has 180 billion language parameters in total. That figure comprises a 125-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts backbone with 6 billion parameters active per token, a 51-billion-parameter n-gram embedding and a 4-billion-parameter multi-token prediction module. The released configuration supports a context of 524,288 tokens. The weights, about 360GB in BF16, are published under the Qwen Community License 1.0, and the company points commercial users to that license's terms.
The company reports results from its own agentic evaluation framework, applied to all models it compared. On the Difficult subset of Anthropic's BioMysteryBench, made up of verifiable problems that domain experts could not solve independently, Fx-Bio-1031 scored 70.59% Pass@5, against 52.94% for Opus-5 and 47.06% for GPT-6-Astra.

items.t: جوجل تتيح لـ Gemini تحليل الإنفاق عبر Google Wallet
items.d: أعلنت جوجل إتاحة ربط Gemini بمحفظة Google Wallet في الولايات المتحدة، مع إمكانية تحليل الإنفاق والاشتراكات وإعداد الميزانيات عند موافقة المستخدم.
items.x:
جوجل تتيح ربط Gemini بمحفظة Google Wallet لتحليل الإنفاق والاشتراكات وإعداد الميزانيات في الولايات المتحدة عبر ربط اختياري للبيانات المالية.
أعلنت شركة جوجل إتاحة ربط مساعد الذكاء الاصطناعي Gemini بخدمة Google Wallet، في خطوة تسمح للمستخدمين بالحصول على تحليلات لعمليات الإنفاق وإعداد الميزانيات ومتابعة الاشتراكات المتكررة بالاعتماد على بياناتهم المالية، دون مغادرة واجهة المحادثة.
وبحسب الإعلان الرسمي للشركة الصادر في 13 نوفمبر 2026، بدأ طرح الربط لمستخدمي تطبيق Gemini في الولايات المتحدة، عبر الويب وأجهزة أندرويد وآيفون. ولم تعلن جوجل موعدًا لتوفير الميزة في بقية الأسواق، بما فيها الدول العربية.
تندرج الميزة ضمن منظومة «الذكاء الشخصي» (Personal Intelligence)، التي تتيح لمساعد جوجل الاستفادة من معلومات بعض الخدمات المرتبطة بحساب المستخدم، بعد الحصول على موافقته. ويمكن استخدام الإشارة @Google Wallet في محادثة Gemini لطرح أسئلة تتعلق بالإنفاق والادخار.
ومن الأمثلة التي عرضتها جوجل إمكانية مراجعة نفقات الأشهر السابقة، وإنشاء رسوم بيانية تفاعلية للميزانية والتدفقات المالية، والتعرّف على الاشتراكات المتكررة، وتنبيه المستخدم إلى ارتفاع أسعار بعض الخدمات، فضلًا عن تقدير ميزانية مناسبة للتسوق أو السفر اعتمادًا على معاملات سابقة.
ولا يقتصر الربط الاختياري على البيانات الموجودة في Google Wallet؛ إذ يستطيع المستخدم ربط بطاقاته وحساباته المصرفية بالمحفظة عبر خدمة Plaid للحصول على صورة أشمل…

items.t: Amazon has a plan to index the world’s online shopping data
items.d: Amazon has plans to build a vault of data on every product sold anywhere on the internet, even products Amazon doesn't sell, and make the information available through its own site, according to Reuters. The project, called the "World…
items.x: Amazon has plans to build a vault of data on every product sold anywhere on the internet, even products Amazon doesn't sell, and make the information available through its own site, according to Reuters . The project, called the "World Product Graph," is meant to make it less likely that shoppers leave Amazon to do their product research on Reddit or Google, and make it more likely shoppers end up at Amazon even if they're searching for a product sold elsewhere. items.t: ما الذي عطّل مايكروسوفت 365؟ تشريح خلل الشبكة وفشل الخوادم
items.d: تقرير تقني معمق يشرح كيف كشف تغيير شبكي خللًا كامنًا في بنية مايكروسوفت، وأدى إلى اختناق الاتصالات الآمنة وفشل فحوص سلامة الخوادم وتعطل خدمات Microsoft 365، مع تسلسل الحادث وخطوات المعالجة وما لم يُحسم بعد.
items.x:
تشريح تقني لعطل Microsoft 365: كيف كشف تغيير شبكي خللًا كامنًا وأدى إلى توقف الخوادم وتعطل Outlook وTeams؟ تسلسل الحادث والإصلاحات بالتفصيل.
أقرت شركة مايكروسوفت بأن العطل الواسع الذي أصاب خدمات Microsoft 365 ابتداءً من الخميس 12 نوفمبر 2026 نشأ من مشكلة أُدخلت خلال ترقية سابقة لسعة الشبكة، ثم ظهرت آثارها بعد تغيير شبكي أحدث. وتكشف تفاصيل التحقيقات التشغيلية أن ما بدا في البداية ارتفاعًا في أحمال الخوادم كان، في جانب أساسي منه، نتيجة لفقدان عدد كبير من الخوادم قدرتها على معالجة الطلبات، وما تبع ذلك من اختلال في توزيع الاتصالات.
وامتد تأثير الحادث من Exchange Online وOutlook إلى وظائف مترابطة داخل Teams وCopilot وSharePoint وأدوات الإدارة والأمن والواجهات البرمجية. وفي أحدث تحديث تفصيلي راجعته «البوابة التقنية»، الصادر مساء الجمعة 13 نوفمبر عند الساعة 22:00 بالتوقيت العالمي، أي الثانية صباح السبت بتوقيت الإمارات، قالت مايكروسوفت إن التعافي أصبح مستقرًا على نطاق واسع، لكنها أبقت الحادث مفتوحًا للمراقبة ومتابعة معالجة البريد الإلكتروني المتراكم.
يعيد هذا التقرير بناء ما جرى داخل البنية التحتية للشركة اعتمادًا على التحديثات التي أصدرتها مايكروسوفت للحادثتين EX1550543 وMO1550821، والمنقولة من لوحة صحة الخدمة المؤسسية عبر سجل جامعة بنسلفانيا، مع الفصل الصريح بين الوقائع التي كشفتها الشركة، والتفسير الهندسي المرجح، والأسئلة التي لم يُجب عنها التحقيق المنشور بعد.
في تحديث الساعة 17:57…

items.t: مستشفيات وبورصات وحكومات.. أبرز الجهات المتضررة من عطل مايكروسوفت العالمي
items.d: امتد عطل مايكروسوفت 365 إلى مستشفيات بريطانية وبورصة يورونكست وحكومات وشركات طيران وشحن، وأوقف معالجة التأشيرات في نيوزيلندا. إليك الجهات المتضررة والخدمات التي استمرت.
items.x:
تعرف على أبرز الجهات المتضررة من عطل مايكروسوفت 365: مستشفيات NHS، وشرطة بريطانيا، ويورونكست، وهجرة نيوزيلندا، وشركات الطيران والشحن.
امتدت تداعيات العطل العالمي في خدمات مايكروسوفت 365، الذي بدأ مساء الخميس 12 نوفمبر 2026، إلى مستشفيات وأجهزة شرطة وهيئات حكومية وبورصات وشركات طيران وشحن دولية، متسببة في تعطيل المراسلات وتأخير معاملات وخدمات يستخدمها ملايين الأشخاص. وأظهرت البيانات الرسمية الصادرة يوم الجمعة أن الضرر تفاوت بين فقدان البريد الإلكتروني وتعليق خدمات رقمية كاملة، فيما واصلت مؤسسات كثيرة تشغيل أنظمتها الأساسية.
وبينما أعلنت مايكروسوفت تقدمًا واسعًا في استعادة الخدمات، أكدت أن بعض العملاء والمناطق ظلوا بحاجة إلى إجراءات استعادة إضافية، وأن رسائل متأخرة كانت لا تزال في طوابير المعالجة. وتأتي هذه المتابعة لاستعراض الجهات المتضررة بالاسم والأثر الموثق لكل منها، بعد أن تناولت تغطية سابقة في البوابة التقنية امتداد العطل إلى الخدمات السحابية وتكاملات تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي.
برز قطاع الصحة البريطاني ضمن أكثر القطاعات التي أبلغت عن مشكلات مباشرة. ووفقًا لحصر نشرته سكاي نيوز يوم الجمعة، أعلنت 47 مؤسسة صحية تابعة لهيئة الخدمات الصحية الوطنية (NHS) على الأقل مواجهة صعوبات مرتبطة بالعطل، خصوصًا في البريد الإلكتروني وبعض الأنظمة الإدارية.
وأكد مستشفى كينغز كوليدج في لندن تعذر إرسال رسائل البريد واستقبالها، لكنه أوضح أن خدمات المرضى والعمليات الجراحية والمواعيد استمرت كالمعتاد.

items.t: Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say
items.d: Nvidia poured tens of billions into AI startups under Huang. Without him at the helm, founders and VCs are bracing for smaller checks and lower valuations.
items.x:
Nvidia poured tens of billions into AI startups under Huang. Without him at the helm, founders and VCs are bracing for smaller checks and lower valuations.
It was the resignation heard across the world. Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s embattled CEO who co-founded and led the company for 33 years, had officially stepped down. “It’s like a bomb went off,” one neocloud founder told TechCrunch when he first heard the news.
Over the last several years, Nvidia has been a prolific investor, pouring tens of billions into startups annually, and participating in 105 rounds this year alone often as the largest investor, according to PitchBook. “If that direction changes, it’ll be a big blow to so many young companies,” said Maria Davidson, founder of Relational Capital.
Huang’s absence leaves the startup ecosystem without one of its biggest champions and with far less capital for now, investors say, which could have a massive impact on dealmaking, valuations, funding, and even competition.
“Nvidia is carrying almost every AI-native startup from application to neocloud,” Dawn Capital’s Shamilla Bankiya told TechCrunch.
Most of the significant decisions to invest in startups often came from Jensen himself, according to Umesh Padval, managing partner at Seligman Ventures.

items.t: خلل في اتصالات المراقبة الجوية يوقف إقلاع الرحلات في الولايات المتحدة
items.d: أمرت إدارة الطيران الفيدرالية الأمريكية بوقف إقلاع الرحلات في أنحاء الولايات المتحدة عقب خلل في اتصالات مراكز المراقبة الجوية الـ22، وسط تحقيق رسمي في السبب.
items.x:
أصدرت إدارة الطيران الفيدرالية الأمريكية أمرًا بوقف إقلاع الرحلات بسبب خلل في اتصالات مراكز المراقبة الجوية الـ22. تفاصيل القرار وتداعياته وما لم يتضح بعد.
أصدرت إدارة الطيران الفيدرالية الأمريكية (FAA) يوم الجمعة 13 نوفمبر 2026 أمرًا بوقف إقلاع الرحلات في المطارات الأمريكية، بعدما أثرت مشكلة في الاتصالات على مراكز مراقبة الحركة الجوية الإقليمية، في اضطراب واسع استدعى إجراءات احترازية لضمان سلامة الطيران.
وبحسب وكالة أسوشيتد برس، امتد تأثير المشكلة إلى مراكز مراقبة الحركة الجوية الإقليمية الـ22 المسؤولة عن توجيه الطائرات بين مناطق البلاد. وأفاد وزير النقل الأمريكي شون دافي بأن الفرق الفنية تعمل على التحقيق في الخلل. ولم يُعلن سبب جذري نهائي للحادث في الإفادات الأولية التي استند إليها هذا التقرير.
أفاد تنبيه مركز قيادة الحركة الجوية رقم 111، الصادر في 13 نوفمبر عند الساعة 20:54 بالتوقيت العالمي المنسق (UTC)، الموافق 00:54 صباح السبت 14 نوفمبر بتوقيت الإمارات، بأن جميع المطارات الأمريكية مشمولة بقرار وقف الإقلاع لأسباب تتعلق بالسلامة. ونص التنبيه على إبقاء الرحلات المغادرة على الأرض حتى إشعار آخر، مع التعامل مع الرحلات الدولية الوافدة وفق كل حالة على حدة.
ولا يعني القرار إنزال الطائرات الموجودة في الجو فورًا؛ فقد استمرت الرحلات الجوية التي كانت قد أقلعت بالفعل في مساراتها، مع السماح لها بالهبوط وفق تعليمات الجهات المختصة.

items.t: مايكروسوفت تكشف السبب التقني لعطل Microsoft 365 وتعلن معالجة الخلل الأساسي
items.d: كشفت مايكروسوفت أن عطل Microsoft 365 ارتبط بمشكلة في ترقية سابقة للشبكة ظهرت بعد تغيير أحدث، وأعلنت معالجة الخلل الأساسي واستمرار التعافي التدريجي للخدمات.
items.x:
كشفت مايكروسوفت أن العطل العالمي لخدمات Microsoft 365 ارتبط بترقية سابقة للشبكة وتغيير أحدث، وأعلنت معالجة المشكلة الأساسية واستمرار تعافي الخدمات.
أعلنت شركة مايكروسوفت أنها عالجت الخلل التقني الأساسي الذي تسبب في اضطراب واسع لخدمات Microsoft 365 بدأ يوم الخميس 12 نوفمبر 2026، وكشفت أن المشكلة نشأت خلال ترقية سابقة للسعة الاستيعابية للشبكة، قبل أن تظهر تداعياتها عقب إجراء تغيير شبكي أحدث. وأكدت الشركة تحقيق تعافٍ واسع للخدمات، مع استمرار العمل على استعادة الوظائف المتأثرة لدى بعض العملاء والمناطق، من دون إعلان انتهاء جميع الآثار في وقت واحد.
ويمثل هذا التفسير تطورًا جديدًا في الحادثة التي عطّلت خدمات Outlook وExchange Online وأثرت في وظائف أخرى ضمن منظومة مايكروسوفت وتكاملات أطراف ثالثة. وكان التركيز خلال الساعات الأولى على الخوادم التي أصبحت غير متاحة والضغط المتزايد على بقية البنية التحتية، قبل أن تعلن الشركة تفسيرها التقني الأحدث.
وفقًا لما نقلته The Verge عن إفادة الشركة، فقد أُدخلت المشكلة خلال ترقية أقدم لقدرة الشبكة، ثم برز أثرها بعد تغيير آخر جرى مؤخرًا. وقالت مايكروسوفت إنها أصلحت الخلل الأساسي وبدأت تسجيل تعافٍ واسع، لكنها واصلت استعادة الخدمة تدريجيًا للتحقق من استقرار الأنظمة مع عودة الضغط عليها.
ولا تعني هذه الإفادة أن كل التفاصيل الهندسية للحادث أصبحت معروفة؛ إذ تعهدت الشركة بنشر مراجعة تفصيلية بعد انتهاء التحقيق.

items.t: FAA expands AI advice to manage air traffic congestion across entire US airspace
items.d: Airlines praised the AI tool, but the air traffic controllers’ union wasn’t involved.
items.x:
The US government has expanded the use of an AI tool for advising air traffic controllers to assist in managing air traffic across the entire national airspace system. Airline executives have voiced support for the rollout, but the US labor union representing air traffic controllers has said it was not involved in designing or testing the AI-driven system.
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says the $875 million SMART system has helped reroute 180 flights since being implemented in airspace over Washington, DC, on September 21. The agency claims that this saved an average of 10 minutes per flight and almost 80 gallons of fuel per flight—and it is apparently hoping such results can be replicated nationwide through the expanded deployment.
“After a successful initial rollout to the National Capital Region in September, the FAA will now use SMART in the airspace of all 22 centers across the country to reduce delays, reduce fuel consumption and improve the travel experience for the flying public,” according to the agency statement posted on November 10.

items.t: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI’s Dots agents make purchases for you
items.d: After launching its Dots AI agents platform earlier this year, OpenAI is launching a wallet for the agents. ChatGPT Wallet is rolling out starting today for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US aged 18 and older using a US billing address and…
items.x:
OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet, which its Dots agents can use to make purchases with your credit or debit cards.
OpenAI says ChatGPT Wallet won’t share your actual credit card info with its AI agents.﻿
After adding a card to the wallet, your Dots agents can use it to buy things in response to your prompts, but they’ll check in with you each time before checking out. OpenAI’s support page says every purchase with ChatGPT Wallet requires a security check with biometric verification like Face ID or a fingerprint scan.
After you review the AI agent’s purchase and sign off on it, OpenAI says that, similar to using tap to pay, Apple Pay, or Google Wallet, it substitutes your credit card details with a payment token, so your actual card info isn’t shared with your Dots agent or the business you’re buying from. Eventually, OpenAI says it expects “users to be able to delegate purchases entirely to their agent by setting clear parameters—such as spending limits, purchase categories, or time periods—and pre-approve those purchases.”
ChatGPT Wallet might not work everywhere. Some retailers have restrictions on AI agents or block them altogether. Earlier this year, Amazon blocked Meta’s Muse agents.

items.t: AI agent startup LangChain hits $3B valuation
items.d: LangChain now claims 7,000 customers of its model and platform agnostic agent management tool LangSmith.
items.x:
LangChain now claims 7,000 customers of its model and platform agnostic agent management tool LangSmith.
Agent management startup LangChain has raised a $300 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation led by CapitalG, with participation from investors, including Singapore’s GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP, and Sapphire Ventures, the company announced on Friday.
That’s more than double its $1.25 billion valuation when it raised $125 million about a year ago, led by IVP.
LangChain began in 2022 as a popular open source project that handled the kinds of tasks that early-stage LLMs found difficult, like searching the web, calling APIs, and interacting with databases. As the frontier AI labs delivered harnesses that now competently do those tasks, LangChain turned its focus toward managing AI agents. It has apparently found its stride in this highly competitive area with a simple message: letting businesses own their own intelligence.
With its open source roots, the startup says its agent creation and management software, LangSmith, is not trying to lock users into any particular model, cloud, or ecosystem, unlike the major clouds or frontier AI labs.

items.t: What’s really at stake in the Jensen Huang saga
items.d: One part of the saga surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang ended on Thursday, when Huang resigned from his position at the top of AI's most important company. But in the coming weeks and months, a much bigger story may be about to unfold. A…
items.x:
One part of the saga surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang ended on Thursday, when Huang resigned from his position at the top of AI's most important company. But in the coming weeks and months, a much bigger story may be about to unfold. A story about Nvidia's dealings in China, about the US government's willingness to turn a lot of blind eyes to protect a powerful ally, and about the very stability of the AI industry as a whole. It's a lot.

The apparently widespread access to Blackwell GPUs among Chinese frontier labs shows the magnitude of the problem facing the leading chip designer. items.t: Build a Robot Pick-and-Place Simulation with SimReady Assets
items.x:
This walkthrough showcases a beverage can pick-and-place task that uses the UR17G arm, Robotiq 2F-140 gripper, and beverage can to compose a scene in Isaac Sim, check their behavior, and run a pick-and-place example with agent-generated controls.
For robotics workflows, SimReady means an OpenUSD asset has been prepared with the properties needed for a defined simulation use case, such as collisions, mass, joints, and joint drives. SimReady Central, an open asset library on Hugging Face, lets you reuse robot and object assets with authored simulation properties and profile-validation evidence. For more about the library and its launch, read the announcement blog.
SimReady Foundation defines what features the OpenUSD asset needs for a simulation use case. Its specifications connect three levels:
For this task, those properties include the arm and gripper’s joints and a beverage can asset collisions and mass. Validation checks these settings against the profile’s requirements. The simulation then tests whether the assembled robot can use them to pick up and move the can.
The UR17G, Robotiq 2F-140, and beverage can packages include the models and their simulation settings.

items.t: OpenAI board member worries an AI "takeover" of society could be months away
items.d: Researcher traces a path from AI reward hacking to potential human extinction.
items.x:
If you go by the current statistics for deaths in the US , it's reasonable to expect that cancer or heart disease will eventually get you. But OpenAI Foundation board member and Alignment Research Center Executive Director Paul Cristiano thinks we should all be worried about another major mortality risk. Speaking at a lecture series this week , Cristiano bluntly told the audience in a Toronto Convention Center, "I think for most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident."
In the opening lecture of a three-part series , Cristiano outlined his worries about the risk of an impending "AI takeover." He defined that as a situation where goal-pursuing AI systems "call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth" and where any human trying to stop them "would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying to stop the US military." Such a situation would likely lead to mass death and perhaps uninhabitable environments for humans, Cristiano said.

items.t: XYBench: Helping with the problem behind the question
items.x:
Truly useful AI assistants need to be able to help users who ask misguided questions—not just users who ask the right question with the right amount of detail. We’re releasing XYBench, a benchmark of 8K+ questions that tests how AI assistants respond to requests based on misconceptions, such as asking how to thicken frosting that keeps sliding off cupcakes when the real problem is that the cupcakes are still too warm to frost. XYBench won the Best Resource Paper Award at EMNLP 2026.
A mismatch between the approach someone asks about and the goal they want to achieve is known as the XY problem: a person wants to accomplish X, assumes a particular approach Y will work, and asks for help with Y. In the cupcake example, the person is so committed to making the frosting stick that they fail to consider the warmth of the cupcake as the true problem to be addressed.
Developed with researchers at Carnegie Mellon, NVIDIA, and Johns Hopkins, XYBench exposes a critical gap in LLMs' ability to troubleshoot problems: recognizing when a user's request is based on an implicit misconception and appropriately redirecting them toward a solution that addresses their actual goal.

Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security.

The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. To accept payment from ChatGPT Wallet, websites need to ensure agents are not inadvertently blocked, and payment and risk systems need to recognize legitimate purchases made by agents. We’re starting with limited availability to ChatGPT Pro users, so we can learn from real-world use and work with businesses, banks, and payment networks to improve compatibility and reliability.

items.t: llama.cpp v1.0.0 : A stronger foundation for the local AI ecosystem
items.x:
llama.cpp makes it possible to run multi-modal LLMs across a wide range of hardware - from consumer-grade local machines to high-end enterprise servers. Through quantization, optimized backends, and a portable C/C++ implementation, we make AI inference accessible at every level of the software stack. We believe this is the most lightweight, versatile and sensible platform for building cross-platform and private AI products.
During the 3.5 years since its inception, the project has grown a lot and many downstream applications already depend on our work. We expect this trend to continue as local AI and privacy become increasingly important in our everyday lives. Every new integration means more developers depending on our library interfaces and therefore having a flexible but stable API is paramount.
Today we release libraries v1.0.0, highlighting our responsibility to those developers. Moving forward, both llama.cpp and ggml will reflect API and ABI incompatibilities with major-version bumps.

items.t: Andrew Yao and Yang Zhilin Co-Author TCSExam as Kimi K3 Adds an Edge to a Graph Record
items.d: TCSExam, co-authored by Andrew Yao and Yang Zhilin, checks AI research in theoretical CS with Lean 4 and program checkers. Kimi K3 found a 124-vertex graph with a record 630 edges.
items.x:
Turing Award winner Andrew Chi-Chih Yao and Moonshot AI founder Yang Zhilin are among the authors of TCSExam, a benchmark that tests whether AI agents can do research in theoretical computer science rather than solve textbook problems. Leiphone reports that this is the first paper the two have co-authored. The paper, posted to arXiv on November 5, also lists Yifan Luo, Zhengying Liu and Yang Yuan. The task sources, Docker build recipes and evaluation tools are on Moonshot AI's GitHub under Apache-2.0.
TCSExam contains 100 expert-reviewed tasks in four tracks:
- Theorem proving: 20 tasks across 13 areas, each requiring a Lean 4 proof. - Solver engineering: 30 tasks requiring reproducible programs. - Constructions: 20 tasks, such as graphs or codes that meet strict constraints. - Open conjectures: 30 tasks, which a model can attack by proving them or finding counterexamples.
Every submission is checked by the Lean kernel or an executable checker, so a convincing write-up alone does not count. A checkpoint system credits partial progress on long proofs but accepts a main theorem only once unproven intermediate assumptions are removed. Proof tasks run under three levels of guidance, and more than 40 candidate theorems were dropped because models solved them during trial runs.

items.t: HiSilicon CS6286 Image Sensor Puts AI On-Chip, Stretching Dashcam Sentry Mode Past Seven Days
items.d: HiSilicon's CS6286 puts a 50 GOPS AI engine inside an 8MP sensor. It spots people with 95%+ accuracy and lets dashcams sleep, stretching sentry mode past seven days.
items.x:
Shanghai HiSilicon has introduced the CS6286, an 8-megapixel image sensor with a small AI engine built into the sensor itself, and says the chip is already in mass production. The company announced it on November 12 and describes the design as integrating sensing, computing and storage. Its main pitch is dashcams that can watch a parked car for days without draining the battery.
The CS6286 uses a 1/1.8-inch optical format with 2.0-micrometer pixels and a physical resolution of 3840 by 2160, and supports native 4K video at 30 frames per second with HDR. HiSilicon's product page lists pixel-level zoned exposure for HDR with fewer motion artifacts, phase-detection autofocus across all pixels using a 2x2 on-chip lens design, MIPI D-PHY output and wafer-level chip-scale packaging. It also positions the chip for mid-range and high-end security cameras.
The AI engine delivers the equivalent of 50 GOPS at INT8. According to HiSilicon, it detects people with more than 95% accuracy in common settings such as parking lots, roadsides and courtyards. The chip ships with a training kit for degradation, retraining and compilation, so customers can define up to three custom target classes and generate model configuration files from their own datasets.
Sentry mode is where the design matters.

Recommendations for designing, running, and reporting safety evaluations, based on our own experiences.
Safety evaluations inform some of the most consequential decisions we make about an AI model, including whether it’s ready to deploy, which safeguards ship alongside it, and what our next round of safety training and research should focus on. When we say a model is “safer than its predecessor,” we mean that it scored better on a set of evals someone built. But a safety claim is only as sound as the eval behind it, and good ones are hard to build.
A safety eval measures a model’s propensity to cause or contribute to harm, whether its response to a request makes harm more or less likely, and how severe that harm would be, rather than measuring specific capabilities. It can cover different types of harm. For example, a user may actively request harmful outputs (such as seeking instructions on how to harm themselves), or they may request outputs that are intended to be harmless, but that come with high risk of unintended harm (such as seeking information on the appropriate dose of a drug).

items.t: Building always-on agents
items.d: Always-on agents run indefinitely, deciding how and when to act across many sessions. This guide walks through their core primitives and how they fit together.
items.x:
Always-on agents run indefinitely, deciding how and when to act across many sessions. This guide walks through their core primitives and how they fit together.
Over the past few months, we’ve seen a resurgence of always-on agents.
Always-on agents are stateful and proactive, meaning they manage context across sessions and take actions without direct supervision. Underneath, they run on the same core loop as other agents. The difference is the surrounding architecture, which is built from primitives that control when the agents wake up, what carries over between runs, and how their work reaches the user.
The resurgence is largely due to recent model advancements, which have made always-on agents more practical to run. First, the latest models have better judgment: they’re more reliable at understanding user intent and knowing when to check in. Second, intelligence is becoming cheaper, with long-horizon tasks benefiting the most. For example, on one long-horizon coding benchmark, Opus 5.5 cost 78% less per solved task than Opus 5, compared with 40% less on typical workloads.
Customers have started to ask us how to integrate this type of experience into their own products.

items.t: Nebius tests the neocloud playbook with $40 billion in planned spending
items.d: Nebius plans to fund its $40 billion AI infrastructure expansion through customer prepayments and loans, even as delays at a Microsoft data center raise questions about its financing model.
items.x:
Nebius plans to fund its $40 billion AI infrastructure expansion through customer prepayments and loans, even as delays at a Microsoft data center raise questions about its financing model.
In its third-quarter earnings call Thursday, the neocloud company Nebius laid out $40 billion in planned spending for 2027, far more than Wall Street had expected. It’s an ambitious plan, but it rests on a string of planned projects that are already starting to show cracks.
Nebius plans to fund the buildout by relying on customer pre-payments and loans backed by customer contracts — essentially using the future value of its data centers to finance their construction. But that can be a risky strategy if those projects get bogged down by delays or cancellations.
“Building at this scale is hard, and delays are part of our industry right now,” CEO Arkady Volozh said during Thursday’s earnings call. “We are not immune.”
The earnings announcement comes on the heels of reports that Microsoft is cooling on neocloud deals that aren’t delivering on time. That’s a problem for companies like Nebius, whose financing strategy is becoming more dependent on repayments.

items.t: Ars Live: What drone attacks on data centers mean for modern life in the cloud

Drone and missile strikes have inflicted unprecedented damage on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East this year, disrupting cloud services for millions of people and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data. This trend represents a new concern for Big Tech companies—but also for governments and everyone else who depends on common digital services in modern life.
To explore what this all means for modern society’s reliance on cloud resilience, I will be hosting a live conversation titled "Drone attacks and data centers: New Risks for Big Tech" on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET with Joseph Jarnecki , a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK defense and security think tank. With Google's recent Argon and Carbon releases, the rollout was staged and began with cybersecurity researchers. Even when general availability began, Google restricted access to users paying for its most expensive AI subscription. items.t: LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B
items.x:
LLMs rely on their context to generate the next set of tokens. Over a long trajectory, the context fills with numerous types of components: a system prompt, past conversation turns, instructions that act on retrieved documents, tool responses or user data, requirements constraining the allowed output, and reasoning chains. The context carries a rich structure, most of which is either implicit to the model or encoded in formats such as JSON that were not designed to be digested by LLMs. This is one of the main reasons LLMs, particularly those on the smaller end of the scale, are brittle and sometimes fail in unexpected ways. The lack of explicit structure can also be exploited by attackers, for example, in the form of prompt injections.
To address this, we developed LLMON (LLM Object Notation, pronounced “lemon”), an LLM-native markup language for explicitly communicating structure and semantics to the models. Semantically coherent components are marked with meaningful tags which are wrapped in reserved special-token delimiters. Data schemas, including nesting, are stated in a way that is unambiguous to a causal LLM.

CHICAGO—Families joined protests in seven cities nationwide on Wednesday, rallying against what they see as Google’s bid to entrench its AI models in schools, turn kids of all ages into Gemini guinea pigs, and hook them on AI.

While Google claimed it was giving schools “more choice, not less”—by turning off Search, Gemini, and Gemini Notebook by default—it would not provide an option that allowed Search without AI. For students, the only way to avoid interacting with AI was to remember to add “-ai” to every query, parents worried.
In Chicago, many families showed up to protest Google, despite cold, rainy weather. Waving signs, dozens of protesters marched up to Google’s downtown office as workers seemed to be leaving for the day, shouting chants like “Hey Google, nice try, we don’t want your Gemini” and “Hey, Google, leave our kids alone!”

items.t: SoftBank’s billion-dollar loss may have put a cap on AI’s natural gas ambitions
items.d: SoftBank lost over $3 billion preordering natural gas turbines to power AI data centers. Here's what the loss means to power markets.
items.x:
SoftBank lost over $3 billion pre-ordering natural gas turbines to power AI data centers. Here's what the loss means to power markets.
SoftBank might not be the first to invest in a hot trend, but when it does, it goes big.
Witness its $30 billion bet on OpenAI in early 2025 or its announcement in February that its SB Energy subsidiary would spend $33 billion on a 9.2-gigawatt natural gas power plant. If you can’t be first, be biggest, I guess.
That philosophy apparently spilled over into procurement, where orders were also supersized. Starting about two years ago, SoftBank reportedly put down deposits on more than 13 gigawatts of turbines, almost 50% more than it needed.
The decision to over-order undoubtedly helped secure turbines and speed up SoftBank’s projects.
“SB Energy did not have a choice except to overbook turbines in the future if they wanted some turbines right away,” Peter Gardett, CEO of Noreva, told TechCrunch via email.
The energy world was caught off guard by the swiftness and magnitude of AI’s rising power demands. Queues for turbine orders now extend into the early 2030s.

Rather than giving consumers yet another photo-editing tool, Phota Labs aims to use advances in AI to automate the editing process so it’s easier for anyone to turn everyday moments into better photos.
A new iOS app called Phota Labs gives users access to a personal AI photo assistant that turns everyday snapshots into images that look like they were taken by a professional photographer, all while preserving the authenticity of the image.
The a16z-backed startup was founded by Cecilia Zhang and Zach Xia, who met at Adobe while working on computational photography products, including Project Indigo, Lightroom, and Photoshop.
The duo saw a gap in the editing tools on the market and believed that although editing tools can be powerful for enhancing photos, they aren’t very effective at fixing a photo that wasn’t captured well in the first place. Phota Labs changes that by focusing on fixing the shot itself while preserving the natural appearances of those in the image.
“Phota is your personal photo assistant that can make great photos for any moment you want to keep before you even ask, which means that it’s a very proactive experience,” Zhang told TechCrunch in an interview.

Today, we’re talking about the Jensen Huang scandal at Nvidia, which is developing so quickly that we had to do an emergency update of this intro minutes before publishing this episode.
Huang just resigned from his position as CEO of Nvidia as news of his affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy, threatened to engulf the company.

The development comes after House Republicans Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford sent Huang a letter on November 4 requesting that he appear before their committees. “Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” Mast said to reporters.

items.t: Five ways Jensen Huang’s ouster from Nvidia could damage the AI industry
items.d: Nvidia's ousted CEO Jensen Huang's downfall isn’t just your run-of-the-mill salacious billionaire sex scandal. He was using his influence to push the AI industry in some very specific ways.
items.x:
Nvidia's ousted CEO Jensen Huang's downfall isn’t just your run-of-the-mill salacious billionaire sex scandal. He was using his influence to push the AI industry in some very specific ways.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s confession that he had an affair (and reports of another one with a direct report) that led the board to oust him on Thursday isn’t just your run-of-the-mill salacious billionaire CEO sex scandal.
In this case, one of his lovers is suspected by the U.S. government of being a spy for China. She’s also an executive of a Singapore-based neocloud that is suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China.
These affairs show undeniably poor judgment by Huang and, I’d argue, unchecked hubris on many levels. Such choices are not only a betrayal of his wife of 40 years, they’re also a liability for his company. Sleeping with any Nvidia partner is bad enough, but he also chose one in a tinderbox of a geopolitical situation. Even if Alice’s company wasn’t suspected of helping Chinese firms evade chip restrictions (and he was somehow unaware of this), it was still exploiting a legal loophole by renting out powerful AI infrastructure to Chinese companies.
It’s those potential national consequences that may land him in a hellscape of ongoing public humiliation.

In the wake of the industry-shaking news of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation on Thursday, U.S. President Donald Trump is floating the idea that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over the position.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that “only one man” could take Huang’s place: Tim Cook of Apple.
Cook stepped down as Apple’s CEO on September 1, 2026, after 15 years running the company, but he’s still very much involved with Apple. While John Ternus took over as Apple’s CEO, Cook transitioned into the role of Executive Chairman of Apple’s board of directors, which sees him continuing to engage with global policymakers and manage international relationships, including Apple’s relations with China.
Trump is not the only one to suggest Cook as a replacement for Huang. Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, Senior Associate Dean for Leadership Studies at Yale School of Management, who studies CEO leadership and corporate governance, penned an op-ed in Time on Wednesday, suggesting Cook should be among the potential candidates.

items.x:
Nvidia CFO Colette Kress is taking over for as an interim replacement for longtime CEO Jensen Huang, who is embroiled in scandal.
The Nvidia Board of Directors announced on Thursday morning that the company’s co-founder and CEO of 33 years, Jensen Huang, has resigned as President, CEO, and member of the Board, effective immediately.
This is a shocking twist for one of the most valuable companies in the world, which designs the chips that make the AI boom possible. Few people would have predicted this turn of events even just a week ago, as Huang has been so central to Nvidia through out the company’s existence that he never even established a succession plan. But Huang has now been ousted after reports that he had affairs with both an alleged Chinese spy and one of his direct reports at Nvidia.
While the company conducts a more thorough search for Huang’s successor, Nvidia CFO and Executive Vice President Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO. But beyond her name and job title, what do we know about the person who will now lead a company worth about $3.8 trillion?
According to Nvidia’s website, Kress has worked at the company since September 2013. Before that, she spent three years as an SVP and CFO of Cisco’s Business Technology Operations Finance organization.

The company said in its latest security advisory that the cybercriminals took Fireworks’ customers’ billing information and some datasets. Fireworks touts tens of thousands of customers worldwide using its platform, including legal tech company Harvey and AI company Cursor.
At least one confirmed affected customer is online document editor and notetaker Notion, which said in a disclosure that the breach affected around 1% of its own customers.

items.t: Baidu’s Robin Li says AI’s next phase is the “intelligent organization,” outlines three principles
items.d: Baidu founder Robin Li said Thursday that the next stage of AI adoption will require companies to redesign how they work. Speaking at Baidu World 2026 in Beijing, he laid out three principles for what he calls an “intelligent…
items.x:
Baidu founder Robin Li said Thursday that the next stage of AI adoption will require companies to redesign how they work. Speaking at Baidu World 2026 in Beijing, he laid out three principles for what he calls an “intelligent organization”: organize work around tasks that cross job boundaries, document employee know-how so teams and AI agents can reuse it, and measure the results of each workflow so it can be improved over time.
Li said jobs would increasingly fall into two broad groups. He described “builders” as people who create products or services and “sellers” as people whose work depends on communication and trust. The distinction was part of his argument that companies could assign work by task as AI takes on more steps across teams.
Li pointed to Baidu’s own operations as an early example. Over the past year, the number of AI agents active daily inside the company rose from about 5,000 to 37,000, while the number of tasks they completed each week increased from 84,000 to more than 1 million, according to Baidu. [TechNode reporting]

items.t: Who could replace Jensen Huang? A highly unscientific list of possible successors
items.d: Nvidia has no succession plan and a CEO in hot water, so we’ve drafted a shortlist.
items.x:
Nvidia has no succession plan and a CEO in hot water, so we’ve drafted a shortlist.
It’s almost inconceivable that Nvidia would fire its rock star CEO. Yet here we are, on the precipice of this happening. Over at Kalshi, Jensen Huang’s odds of surviving the week are sitting at a lowly 30%. Even though he built one of the world’s most valuable — and, many would argue, dangerously powerful — companies, the tides have completely turned against him. He has confessed to an extramarital affair, but as of Wednesday afternoon it isn’t even clear whom he meant: Alice Huang, the Chinese executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of spying for her country, or Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia executive who reports to him and who, five sources told The New York Times in an explosive new report, was also a paramour.
Even if Huang is pushed out as CEO, the board members he has made very rich are unlikely to cut him loose entirely. Barring another shoe dropping, they could keep him on as chairman, a role Nvidia doesn’t currently have. But someone still has to run the company, and there’s no apparent succession plan, which leaves us, like everyone else, to speculate while we wait to see what happens next.

Tencent has launched a standalone AI search product called Yuanbao Search, Tencent Cloud announced on November 11. It is available by typing so.qq.com into any browser's address bar, and users of the latest QQ Browser can choose it as their search engine in settings. "Yuanbao Search" is a direct translation of the Chinese name. The product page is in Chinese only, and Tencent's official English name for it could not be found.
According to Tencent, Yuanbao Search rebuilds the whole search pipeline on the large-model capabilities behind its Yuanbao assistant, from query understanding through retrieval and ranking to how answers are put together. It draws on an index of hundreds of billions of pages, and its coverage includes the open web, Tencent ecosystem content such as WeChat Official Accounts, WeChat Channels and Tencent News, and academic literature.
Tencent says results give priority to authoritative institutions and official sources, with 157 such sources integrated and citations shown. Ads are clearly separated from answers, and a "collapse ads" option folds the whole ad block away. For academic content, the product summarizes a paper's conclusions in plain language while keeping the original evidence, and translates English titles and abstracts with one click.

items.t: AgiBot Open-Sources LIFE, a Lifelong Embodied AI Framework Built Around RoboBeats Models
items.d: AgiBot's open-source LIFE gives robots continuous sensing via RoboBeats models, reanalyzable memory and reusable tools. Its own tests show 60.5% on SSS-Bench and faster day-long recall.
items.x:
AgiBot has released LIFE ("Learning to Live: A Step Toward Lifelong Embodied Intelligence"), a framework meant to keep a robot perceiving and remembering between tasks rather than resetting after each one. The paper was posted to arXiv on October 30. The code is on GitHub under Apache-2.0, and inference code and weights for RoboBeats models at 0.8B, 2B and 4B parameters followed on November 3. The SSS-Bench evaluation data is under a noncommercial CC BY-NC 4.0 licence. The models are built on Qwen3.5 checkpoints of the same sizes and are hosted on Hugging Face under an individual account linked from AgiBot's repository.
LIFE has three parts working alongside an agent driven by a multimodal large model. RoboBeats is a lightweight decision model that tracks conditions described in natural language, about what the robot sees. Rather than generating text for each frame, it reads true/false scores, and many conditions share the same visual input and cached computation. AgiBot calls this continuous sensing a "heartbeat". Plastic Memory stores raw frames alongside structured JSON records, so the originals can be reanalyzed later when new questions arise, instead of relying only on summaries written at the time.

items.t: The Definitive Fine-Tuning Guide for 3D Generation Models
items.x:
We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
TLDR; In this blog, we provide fine-tuning scripts and containers to fine-tune TRELLIS.2, a popular 3D model on your 3D assets, that can run both locally and on Hugging Face Jobs. If you are interested in fine-tuning, you can use our scripts with few arguments (assuming you updated your dataset to Hugging Face Hub) or tinker with them yourself with this repository. If you want to learn more, we go through how the script works. Let’s go!
3D generation has many uses in robotics, simulation, media, and entertainment. In these fields, it is difficult to make generated objects obey strict rules and standardize model and data representations. There are many file formats, such as GLB and PLY. There are also many representations, such as neural radiance fields (NeRFs) and 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS). Each one has different advantages and disadvantages.
TRELLIS introduced a common internal representation, called a unified latent representation. Its decoders convert this representation into 3D models in the required output format.

items.t: AlphaGenome 2: Deciphering how cells read DNA to better understand disease
items.d: Predicting how DNA sequences and their variations impact specific human cell types and disease.
items.x:
AlphaGenome 2 is our next-generation DNA sequence model that bridges single-cell biology and human genetics, predicting how variants affect human cell types.
Our next-generation DNA sequence model bridges single-cell biology and human genetics, predicting how genetic variants affect hundreds of human cell types.
Today, we are announcing AlphaGenome 2, our next-generation model that predicts how DNA sequences and their variations impact specific human cell types, giving scientists a powerful new tool to uncover the cellular drivers of disease.
Cells are the building blocks of life. Every cell in our body carries the same DNA blueprint, yet each cell type and state—like a heart muscle cell or an immune cell fighting an infection—switches different genes on or off to do its job. Global efforts like the Human Cell Atlas are mapping this gene expression for millions of cells, but it is still an unsolved challenge to predict how subtle DNA variations affect this expression in cells, which is a key driver of human traits and disease.
Last year, we launched AlphaGenome to predict how DNA variants affect molecular activity across broad tissues.

items.t: Google DeepMind just mathematically verified key parts of Signal
items.d: The four-week project hints that AI could make formal verification far more practical.
items.x:
Google DeepMind researchers used agentic AI to mathematically prove, or “formally verify,” a number of the Signal protocol’s key cryptographic guarantees—a landmark development for the widely used cryptography and AI itself.
Conducted as a sort of proof-of-concept project in just four weeks, the work is significant in two ways. It serves as further independent validation of the cryptography that protects massive quantities of the world's communications on platforms like the Signal app , Google Messages, and WhatsApp. And it demonstrates Google DeepMind's formal verification capabilities using a new AI framework called AlphaProof Code.
More broadly, AI-aided formal verification is having a moment, but it is unclear how practical it will be for widespread use and how effective it can be at securing large amounts of code. Proponents of formal verification have long referred to it as a sort of holy grail in software security, because it uses math to check and validate that software is functioning as intended—in other words, that it doesn't have critical vulnerabilities.

items.t: Plurai wants to help AI agents work better using the same approach that helped get self-driving cars to roads
items.d: Like the end-to-end models trained to drive cars, AI agents are probabilistic systems operating in unpredictable environments.
items.x:
Like the end-to-end models trained to drive cars, AI agents are probabilistic systems operating in unpredictable environments.
AI agents are all the rage, but they’re not quite as capable as their purveyors would have you believe.
Efforts to benchmark agents tasked with complex work show that they aren’t typically reliable enough to function without close supervision. LiveBench 2.0 shows Claude Fable 5.2 and ChatGPT-6 Astra succeeding on 82.9 and 75.6 out of 100 tasks, respectively, and an effort by the AI infrastructure company EON to test agents in a simulated corporate environment found the most successful model tested, Claude Opus 4.8, performed tasks at 76.8% accuracy.
Now, a startup known as Plurai wants to boost those numbers with the same techniques that put self-driving cars on the street: Simulations using synthetic data based on a company’s own digital systems, meant to prepare models to tackle difficult edge cases.
Co-founders Ilan Kadar and Elad Levi previously worked for Nexar, which develops autonomous driving technology.

items.t: جامعة محمد بن زايد للذكاء الاصطناعي تطلق نموذج «بان 2» لمحاكاة الواقع
items.d: أطلق معهد النماذج التأسيسية بجامعة محمد بن زايد للذكاء الاصطناعي نموذج «بان 2» مفتوح المصدر لمحاكاة العالم وتوقع نتائج الأفعال عبر الفيديو.
items.x:
جامعة محمد بن زايد للذكاء الاصطناعي تطلق بان 2 (PAN 2)، نموذجًا مفتوح المصدر لمحاكاة العالم وتوقع نتائج الأفعال بالفيديو، مع إتاحة الشيفرة والأوزان.
أعلن معهد النماذج التأسيسية التابع لجامعة محمد بن زايد للذكاء الاصطناعي في أبوظبي إطلاق نموذج «بان 2» (PAN 2) مفتوح المصدر لمحاكاة الواقع، بهدف مساعدة أنظمة الذكاء الاصطناعي على توقع نتائج الأفعال والتخطيط لها عبر محاكاة مرئية، بدلًا من الاعتماد على التجربة المباشرة وحدها.
ووفقًا لبيان صحافي أصدرته الجامعة اليوم، يستطيع النموذج تلقي مشهد أولي ووصف نصي لفعل معين، ثم توليد مقطع فيديو يتنبأ بما يمكن أن يحدث لاحقًا، بالاستناد إلى العلاقات الفيزيائية والزمانية والمكانية التي يتعلمها. ويصف الباحثون هذه الآلية بأنها «الاستدلال بالمحاكاة»، إذ تتيح اختبار سيناريوهات افتراضية قبل تنفيذها في العالم الحقيقي.
يجمع النموذج بين مستويين من الاستدلال؛ أولهما الاستدلال المفاهيمي، وفيه يحدد نموذج لغوي كبير تسلسل الأحداث والأفعال وحركة الكاميرا والتوقيت المتوقع لكل منها. أما المستوى الثاني فهو الاستدلال الإدراكي، إذ يحوّل نموذج انتشار مخصص لتوليد الفيديو هذه الأوصاف إلى مشاهد مرئية تتضمن تفاصيل الحركة والتفاعلات الفيزيائية.
وأوضح المعهد أنه درّب نموذج توليد الفيديو من الصفر باستخدام مقاطع واقعية اختيرت بناءً على ما تتضمنه من ديناميكيات فيزيائية، وليس على جاذبيتها البصرية.

items.t: ChatGPT Plus for veterans and servicemembers
items.d: More than 20,000 veterans and transitioning service members have claimed a free year of ChatGPT Plus. See how they use it to prepare for civilian careers.
items.x:
More than 20,000 veterans and transitioning service members have claimed a free year of ChatGPT Plus. See how they use it to prepare for civilian careers.
In the past year, more than 20,000 transitioning servicemembers and veterans have claimed a year of ChatGPT Plus at no cost after being offered free access by OpenAI. That milestone gives us a chance to look at how veterans are using AI to prepare for civilian careers and to figure out what comes next for themselves and their families.
The effort started with veterans who work here at OpenAI, people who use these tools every day and know firsthand how challenging the transition can be. Beyond the free access, OpenAI Academy and our community partners have hosted more than a dozen trainings for nearly 1,000 members of the military community, with seven more⁠(opens in a new window) scheduled before the year ends.
Leaving the military often means stepping into an unfamiliar job market and working out how years of service translate into a civilian role.

items.t: Alibaba Folds Qoder's Harness Into Qwen Code 1.0 Preview and Open-Sources the Combined Agent Core
items.d: Alibaba's Qwen Code 1.0 Preview opens Qoder's harness as an embeddable agent core, with an event bus that scales from one process to many nodes and centralized MCP and sandbox management.
items.x:
Alibaba announced Qwen Code 1.0 on November 11, merging the agent "harness" built in its Qoder coding product into the open-source Qwen Code project. The harness is the layer that connects a model, its tools and the execution process, and Alibaba says developers can now embed it in their own products. Qwen Code 1.0 Preview is open on a separate branch of the QwenLM/qwen-code repository, and the existing stable branch stays. GitHub lists a v1.0.0-preview pre-release dated November 11 alongside the current 0.27 line, and shows the project under Apache-2.0.
According to Alibaba's description, relayed by IT Home, version 1.0 starts from an in-process, in-memory event bus and extends a unified event model toward distributed operation. Intake, scheduling and execution are layered, and a "brain and hand separation" keeps reasoning orchestration and tool execution under independent management. The aim is to move from one process hosting several sessions to multiple nodes hosting many more, while keeping the existing entry points and return paths.
Alibaba lists four practical effects. Processing units for reasoning, memory and tools can be plugged in around events with less intrusion into the main execution flow.

items.t: Nvidia’s crisis has corporate governance experts reaching for the popcorn
items.d: The governance experts we talked to say nobody has seen anything like what's unfolding right now.
items.x:
The governance experts we talked to say nobody has seen anything like what's unfolding right now.
Nvidia’s stock sank 5.47% on Tuesday, following a 4% drop on Monday, a loss of about 9.5% in two days, even though there wasn’t much news out of the company. CEO Jensen Huang has reportedly been trying to conduct business as usual after admitting an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom U.S. intelligence agencies believe was spying for China. The biggest development seemed to be that Nvidia’s board hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct its investigation.
What comes next is mostly a guessing game, even for the people who study how boards are supposed to handle crises. Two corporate governance professors, Ann Lipton of the University of Colorado and Todd Henderson of the University of Chicago, say there is no real precedent for a CEO caught up in a suspected honeypot. And while they have views on what the investigation should ask, like everyone else, they’re watching to see how it plays out.
“There have actually been affair cases and sexual harassment cases,” Lipton said, but was quick to add that she doesn’t know of previous cases that also involve potential national security compromises.

items.t: Hongguo is booming. What does that mean for Douyin?
items.d: On Nov. 10, Douyin Group Vice President Li Liang cautioned creators against rushing into AI short dramas, citing Hongguo hit Armed Into the Song Dynasty as an example of the experience and resources needed to produce a hit. Since its…
items.x:
On Nov. 10, Douyin Group Vice President Li Liang cautioned creators against rushing into AI short dramas, citing Hongguo hit Armed Into the Song Dynasty as an example of the experience and resources needed to produce a hit. Since its August debut, the series has expanded to about 1,000 episodes across 10 seasons, with cumulative views surpassing 12 billion by Nov. 7, according to The Paper .
The comments come as Hongguo reaches a new milestone. The short-drama app had 430 million users in September, overtaking ByteDance’s AI chatbot Doubao to become its second-largest app after Douyin, according to QuestMobile .
Hongguo’s rapid growth may suggest that ByteDance is finding another way to capture viewers’ entertainment time. But what is drawing audiences to short dramas, and what does their rise mean for Douyin?
A recent 36Kr commentary draws a parallel with Douyin’s early success: short videos gained ground as traditional TV comedy struggled to find fresh material and talent.

items.t: China accelerates data center expansion as the West faces mounting opposition
items.d: As the global AI industry races to secure computing power, data center construction is facing a new set of challenges. Since the second half of 2026, opposition to data center projects has emerged in multiple parts of Europe and the US…
items.x:
As the global AI industry races to secure computing power, data center construction is facing a new set of challenges.
Since the second half of 2026, opposition to data center projects has emerged in multiple parts of Europe and the US. Rising electricity costs, community resistance and disputes over resource allocation have brought some projects to a standstill.
China, by contrast, continues to push ahead with its computing infrastructure expansion, following a development strategy centered on national computing hubs and coordinated growth between eastern and western regions.
AI boom drives faster data center construction in China
A look at China’s computing capacity offers a glimpse of the scale of this expansion. As of June 2026, China had 15.56 million standard data center racks in operation, while its intelligent computing capacity reached 2,185 EFLOPS, up 177% year on year, making it the world’s second-largest market by this measure.
The rapid growth in computing demand is closely linked to the boom in China’s large language model (LLM) industry. Over the past two years, daily token usage by domestic LLMs has increased more than 1,000-fold.

items.t: BotPsy: On-Device Personal Assistant with a Sub-Billion-Parameter Agentic Language Model
items.x:
Frontier cloud LLMs carry high operational costs that can fluctuate unexpectedly, and relying on such third-party models introduces vulnerabilities, as providers can modify, deny, or deprecate access at any time. Furthermore, proprietary models offer limited customization for specific workflows, while posing risks to privacy, data control, and transparency. Besides, not every task demands frontier-level intelligence: small, specialized agents can be equally capable on specific tasks and significantly cheaper to run, since many routine or smaller workloads can be processed efficiently on-device. As intelligence per parameter continues to improve rapidly, we aim to stand at the forefront of this shift toward performant, privacy-focused, self-hosted models.
Tether AI Research introduces BotPsy, a 0.8B-parameter model introduce BotPsy, a 0.8B-parameter model designed for function calling and agentic workflows, built on top of Qwen3.5-0.8B and suitable for on-device deployment. BotPsy is a "personal assistant" that uses tools to perform a variety of simple tasks for the user, in domains such as web search & research, travel & lifestyle, commerce & finance, business & customer operations, device & vehicle control, files & documents, calendar, and email & messaging.

items.t: How AI Helps Recyclers Turn Mixed Waste Into Reusable Material
items.d: Vision AI and robotics pick what’s worth recovering out of conveyor belts of used clothing, bottles and mixed recyclables, diverting thousands of tons of materials from landfills.
items.x:
Vision AI and robotics pick what’s worth recovering out of conveyor belts of used clothing, bottles and mixed recyclables, diverting thousands of tons of materials from landfills.
As world leaders gather for COP31 in Türkiye, the event’s emphasis on zero waste puts a practical challenge in focus: how to keep products and materials in use for longer. Globally, less than 7% of the materials entering the economy come from recycled or reused sources. Municipal solid waste generation accounts for over 2 billion tons of trash per year — a figure that could nearly double by 2050.
AI and robotics are helping change this trajectory, as innovators around the globe improve sorting to recover resources that would otherwise end up in landfills.
“A more circular economy relies on making better use of what we already have,” said Josh Parker, head of sustainability at NVIDIA. “AI can help us understand what’s in a waste stream, identify what can be recovered and automate the work of sorting it.

items.t: DIYgod Open-Sources Pinky, an MCP Layer That Lets AI Agents Operate Real iPhones and Android Phones
items.d: DIYgod's Pinky, open-sourced under Apache-2.0, lets MCP-compatible AI agents operate real iPhones and Android phones with gateway-enforced approvals, logs and a human takeover option.
items.x:
Developer DIYgod has open-sourced Pinky, a desktop app that lets AI coding and general agents operate a real iPhone or Android phone through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), with the user watching and able to approve or block risky steps. The GitHub repository, released under Apache-2.0, was created on November 6. According to a Chinese AI outlet whose report ran on Tencent News, a post announcing it drew about 220,000 views on X and the project passed 1,000 GitHub stars within 25 hours. GitHub showed roughly 1,700 stars on November 11, and the outlet reported 30 releases in a single day.
Pinky runs on macOS, Windows and Linux. The README says it drives Android 10 to 17 and iPhones on iOS 17.4 or later, with a helper installed once from Xcode on iOS 17.4 to 26. Agents named include Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex and Cursor, plus any MCP-compatible tool or script. Pinky carries no model of its own and acts as the link between agent and phone.
Android phones can pair over Wi-Fi after an initial cable connection, and on Android 13 and later Pinky uses a hidden second screen so the agent can work while the phone's own display stays locked. On iOS the agent shares the phone's main screen. A Tailscale option reaches Android phones outside the local network.

items.t: MiniMax Opens Weights for H3-Image, a 16-Megapixel Text-to-Image and Editing Model Run in Six Steps
items.d: MiniMax released H3-Image weights: a 33.1B diffusion transformer that makes 16MP images in six steps and edits with up to 16 references. A community licence sets a territory.
items.x:
MiniMax has released MiniMax-H3-Image with open weights, a text-to-image and image-editing model derived from its H3 family. The release came late on November 10, and the weights are on Hugging Face. MiniMax says the model produces a roughly 16-megapixel image, 4096 by 4096 at 1:1, in under 10 seconds, and describes that as about five times faster than the market norm for that resolution.
According to the model card, a single checkpoint handles both text-to-image and editing of one or more reference images, and accepts up to 16 references. The diffusion transformer has 33.1 billion parameters, uses the H3 design without the audio layers and is distilled to six sampling steps without classifier-free guidance. Its text encoder is the MiniMax-H3 text encoder, which is a separate download. MiniMax lists output sizes up to 6272 by 2688 without an upscaler. The BF16 checkpoint is 68.65 GB, and an optional prompt-expansion model called MiniMax-H3-Image-PE is 17.9 GB.
MiniMax calls the model's instruction following the strongest among open-source image models and says it avoids the familiar "AI look". Those are the company's own claims, and no independent comparison was in the source material.

items.t: Huawei's openJiuwen Unveils TTSE, an Agent Framework That Splits Environment Facts From Tips
items.d: openJiuwen's TTSE sorts agent experience into environment facts and conditional tips. The team reports 97.8% on ALFWorld and cuts office-task tool calls in demos; results are its own.
items.x:
openJiuwen, Huawei's open-source agent platform, has introduced TTSE (Two-Track Self-Evolution), a framework that lets an AI agent learn from its past tasks by sorting what it learns into two kinds. QbitAI reported on November 10 that it is described in an arXiv paper submitted on September 21 and is now built into openJiuwen's WorkSwarm office agent.
The idea, borrowed from cognitive science, is to separate declarative from procedural knowledge. FACT records what the environment is like, such as where files sit or how data is formatted. TIP records what to do under stated conditions. Anything the system cannot classify defaults to TIP, so unverified habits are less likely to be treated as facts.
TTSE starts from an empty rule base, runs a first batch of tasks and induces initial rules from the traces. In later batches the agent loads the earlier rules, runs tasks, then blames misleading rules, retires them, resolves contradictions by merging them into conditional tips, and induces new rules. Retired rules are kept with reasons for traceability.
The team tested five benchmarks, three runs each.

items.t: Token Pooling-Aware Training for Multi-Vector Embedding Models
items.x:
We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
Multi-vector embedding models give each query token its own opportunity to find a match in a document. This makes them wonderfully expressive for search, but those document vectors add up quickly. A corpus with millions of documents can contain hundreds of millions of vectors!
Token pooling makes these representations smaller by merging similar token vectors. The more aggressively I compress them, however, the easier it becomes to lose something useful. Pooling-aware training teaches the encoder to preserve the information that matters when its vectors are merged, helping you retrieve better from the same storage budget.
In this post, I'll explain how pooling works, train a model for compressed retrieval with Sentence Transformers, and explore the resulting quality and storage tradeoff. With pool_factor=4, my normally trained model retains 94.6% of its unpooled NanoBEIR nDCG@10, with a 4x reduction in document vectors. Token pooling-aware training raises that retention to 97.8% at the same storage budget!

items.t: Grok Build coding agent leaks oodles of confidential info, some belonging to SpaceXSI

items.x:
Grok Build, the vibe-coding agent from SpaceXSI, is leaking data—some of it proprietary business information and other sensitive secrets—from thousands of its users, including the very same Elon Musk-owned company that offers the platform, new research shows.
The information is revealed through links allowing Grok Build users to share their apps with others. Grok takes steps to randomize the URLs so only people who know the exact URL can access the data stored there. A design decision by developers of the platform, however, completely torpedoes that objective and makes it possible for anyone to enumerate thousands of live Grok Build projects. Except in rare cases, clicking those links opens the app and reveals all data associated with it.
Research from security firm Claroc shows that the exposed data includes things like internal business plans, ad proposals, medical exam results, galley checklists from a celebrity cruise line, and employee names and ID numbers. Ironically, some of the sensitive data comes from two-dozen apps built by SpaceXSI (the name of the now-merged SpaceX and xAI) itself.

New York is preparing to enforce its sweeping AI safety law, requiring major developers like OpenAI and Anthropic to register, disclose safety practices, and report critical incidents or face fines.
New York is gearing up to enforce one of the country’s most significant AI safety laws. The state opened a registration portal Tuesday, with which large frontier AI developers like Anthropic and OpenAI will be required to register by January 1, 2027.
The RAISE Act, New York’s safety and transparency bill, kicks in at the start of the year. It mandates that large frontier developers — companies with more than $500 million in annual revenue — have to publish safety frameworks on their websites, report critical safety incidents within 72 hours, and issue public model transparency reports.
The newly formed Office of Digital Innovation, Governance, Integrity, and Trust (DIGIT) will implement the RAISE Act and oversee large frontier AI labs.

items.t: What happens to mathematics when AI becomes an oracle?
items.d: Mathematician Steven Strogatz discusses his new book, Big Math: The Hidden Codes That Run Our World .
items.x:
Our modern world runs on math, from social media algorithms, package delivery, and weather prediction to medical imaging and machine learning. The rise of computers helped fuel its dominance, enabling us to work with increasingly large numbers that would otherwise be beyond the capacity of our finite human brains. But with the rise of large language models, AI chatbots, and, soon, quantum computing, so-called "big math" is beginning to outstrip its creators entirely. What that means , and how we might adapt, is the focus of a new book, Big Math: The Hidden Codes That Run Our World , by applied mathematicians Steven Strogatz and Alex Townsend.
Strogatz is perhaps best known in his field for his co-authorship of a seminal 1998 paper with Duncan Watts on the collective dynamics of small-world networks. He has also studied chaos theory as applied to physics, the geometry of supercoiled DNA, and the biological collective oscillators, such as swarms of synchronously flashing fireflies and crickets that chirp in unison.

items.t: PSI is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery
items.d: PSI used an unreleased Anthropic model to answer a fundamental question about quantum computing that scientists have pursued for nearly two decades.
items.x:
PSI used an unreleased Anthropic model to answer a fundamental question about quantum computing that scientists have pursued for nearly two decades.
David Turturean, a recent MIT graduate and a member of the technical staff at the startup lab Physical Superintelligence (PSI), used early access to Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 model to solve an eighteen-year-old problem about quantum computing.
“I’m totally accepting the idea that this might be the last paper I ever put out,” Turturean, who deferred plans to pursue a master’s at MIT’s prestigious computer science and AI lab to join PSI, told TechCrunch. “In a few months, like, why would you even put out a paper?”
The problem in question, the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, concerns the ability of quantum computers to solve problems faster than classical ones. Scott Aaronson, one of the two researchers who posed the problem, writes that he doesn’t quite understand the proof, but that he believes it’s correct because it was autoformalized in Lean, a coding language for math, and explained by a team of top researchers with whom PSI shared the solution.
The solution appears to close the door on one avenue quantum computers could follow to solve certain difficult problems at high speed, but not all of them.

Essentially, it takes your instructions and uses live video to plan how the robot can accomplish the task. The other main component is the vision-language-action (VLA) that actually generates robot actions, like moving an actuator—that's Gemini Robotics, which has been bumped to version 2.5.
DeepMind says that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity. The model was evaluated across more than 200 activities, including serving food with tongs and using a pipette, as you would see in a laboratory.

items.t: Ukraine’s fiber-optic drones get squeezed by AI data center demand
items.d: Ukraine competes with Russia and data centers for China’s optical fiber supply.

Impervious to battlefield jamming, drones physically connected to human operators by miles of fiber-optic cables have become such a common weapon of war in Ukraine that trees and fields are strewn with tangled cables thinner than fishing lines. But importing such fiber-optic material from China has become more costly as drone warfare’s needs compete with global demand from AI data centers for the same limited supply—and so Ukrainian drone makers have been adapting.
Since the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022, the Ukrainians have been forced out of necessity to continually develop battlefield innovations involving first-person view (FPV) quadcopter drones and other heavier types of drones. But it was the Russian military that first deployed unjammable fiber-optic drones to repel Ukrainian forces’ cross-border incursion into the Kursk Oblast in 2024.

items.t: Introducing AlphaProof Code: a breakthrough in verifying complex software at depth
items.d: AlphaProof Code agents wrote three million lines of proofs in Lean to verify Signal’s core encryption.
items.x:
AlphaProof Code agents wrote over three million lines of machine-checked proof in Lean to verify the core cryptographic protections in Signal down to machine instructions.
How Google DeepMind researchers built a new agentic framework that formally verified the code of Signal’s cryptographic protocol — long considered to be a grand security challenge
Today, we’re sharing a milestone in software security long considered to be a grand security challenge: Google DeepMind researchers guided AI agents to mathematically prove key security properties of the actual code underlying the Signal protocol, the technology that protects billions of private conversations in apps like Signal and Google Messages.
This breakthrough discovery was made using AlphaProof Code, a novel agentic framework for formal verification at unprecedented depth that combines human expertise with AI agents. Formal verification—mathematically proving code runs correctly without flaws—is the highest standard of security assurance; however, it is difficult and often labor-intensive.
Our work marks the first time AI has been used to formally verify a widely deployed cryptographic protocol at this depth.
